newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends higher, strong spot month gains.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends higher, strong spot month gains.

text.p: COMEX copper ended higher Wednesday, helped by some shortcovering ahead of U.S. Thanksgiving when COMEX will be closed Thursday and Friday and the closely watched LME stock report due Friday.
"There was some shortcovering as the holiday period is a long one, but beyond that supplies are tight," said Bette Raptopoulos of Prudential Securities.

Spot December settled 2.10 cents higher at 110.30 cents a lb, reflecting tightness in key LME December dates which prompted some concern among traders as large short positions reach crunch time amid six-year low exchange inventories.
Most-active March made more modest gains, ending up 0.70 cent at 104.80 cents. Volume was estimated at 12,000 lots, down sharply from Tuesday's official 24,978 lots.
Spot copper closed at its highest since just before Sumitomo announced huge red metal trading losses mid-June.
The LME December premium over COMEX established on Tuesday firmed to five cents by Wednesday's close. LME December ended at the equivalent of 115.30 cents per pound.
Traders said the switch to an LME premium was likely to draw material into LME warehouses that would have gone into COMEX or was already in the New York exchange's depots.

Raptopoulos said exchange stocks were at very low levels. "In normal times, the copper price would have been much, much higher, about $1.40 per pound at least," she added. "That perception, and concern that the market may rally Friday when nobody is trading, may have encouraged the shortcovering."
COMEX's Wednesday session ended a hour earlier at 1300 EST. The exchange will reopen Monday.
